text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA:
- Brokers from more than 130 Romanian brokerage houses can enter "The Broker of the Year" competition launched by National Investment Fund, awarding 100 million lei in prize money.

- Trade unions from the Petrotel refinery in Ploiesti, who say their plant pays its dues to the state budget, want the government to admit that its closure is a political decision agreed with the IMF, says a newspaper report.
- The ceiling for guarantees on individual bank deposits has doubled to 20.12 million lei, on the back of inflation.
- Talks on the sale of nearly 51 percent in cement maker Romcim will start tomorrow.
- Only farmers who had ensured their crops did not suffer damages from this summer's floods, the newspaper says.

- More than 560,000 hectares of crop land have been submerged by floods. Of 2.3 million hectares under wheat, 196,404 hectares have been damaged, the newspaper quotes farming ministry sources as saying.
ADEVARUL
- Trade union leaders and finance ministry experts have agreed to raise minimum monthly pay to 300,000 lei starting October 1.
- The State Ownership Fund (FPS) wants Petrobrazi and Rafo refineries to be included in the new National Oil Company, FPS head Sorin Dimitriu said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper quotes Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu as saying that none of the 17 state firms with chronic losses will be removed from the list of companies slated for winding up.
- By the end of August, winding up procedures will be launched for another 10 plants with big losses, the newspaper quotes FPS president Sorin Dimitriu as saying.
General:
ADEVARUL
- Labour unions from the cement-making sector will picket the government offices starting today, to protest against industry restructuring.
- Convicts at the Gherla jail refuse to return to work in the furniture plant at their penitentiary, the newspaper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper runs an interview with Romania's ambassador to the United States, Mircea Geoana, on improved ties between Bucharest and Washington.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- More than 500,000 tourists are expected to come to Romania to watch the total eclipse of the Sun in August 1999, the newspaper quotes the director of the Bucharest Astronomical Institute as saying.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
